clue.text: Trample crop in field

parts.note: to pad is to tread or walk heavily, so trample gives pad
to dock is to cut short, as a tail is cropped

explanation.surface: A farmer flattens the harvest growing in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small enclosed pasture, a kind of field for horses.

clue.text: Take part in two sports, showing depression

parts.note: to punch is what a boxer does, and to bowl is what a cricketer or bowls player does
to punch is what a boxer does, and to bowl is what a cricketer or bowls player does

explanation.surface: A sports enthusiast doing two events ends up feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood, but here it is a hollow in the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl-shaped hollow in hills is a geographical depression.

clue.text: Trouble intensified in plant

parts.note: to dog someone is to trouble or plague them
rose means increased or grew stronger

explanation.surface: A problem worsened inside a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' could be a factory, but it is the wild rose of hedgerows.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild briar of European hedges is a flowering shrub, so a plant.

clue.text: Keep your eye here and fly with it

definitions.meaning: the instruction to watch the ball in sport: keep your eye on it
fly means sharp or alert, and to be with it is to be alert and up to date

explanation.surface: Advice to watch closely and soar along with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and quick is the idiom; the literal phrase is where a batsman's gaze should rest.

clue.text: Continue to look up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: peek means a quick look

explanation.surface: Carry on searching overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going or carry on is to continue.

clue.text: Longs to shift seconds in casual wear

indicators.note: shift says one piece of the garment's name is picked up and set down somewhere else in it

parts.note: T-shirts are everyday informal tops

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to change quickly into something comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' moves the S of TSHIRTS from second place to fifth, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave it, the figurative sense of being dry and wanting drink.

clue.text: Lay and clerical wear for runner -

parts.note: to table a document is to lay it before a meeting
the cloth is the clergy's dress and so the clergy itself

explanation.surface: Ordinary churchgoers and priests in robes go in for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like lay (not clergy) set against 'clerical', but it is the verb. A runner is a strip of fabric along a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A table runner is a long decorative strip laid on a table, a narrow form of the covering.

clue.text: It's not fitting to drop off in it

indicators.note: in places the doze within the two letters of it

parts.note: to nap is to drop off, fall asleep briefly

explanation.surface: Falling asleep at an event is improper behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate.

clue.text: 'Agent who has to wait for a kipper?

definitions.meaning: a spy planted to lie dormant until activated
someone who kips, or sleeps; the question mark flags the jokey coinage

explanation.surface: A spy waits patiently for a smoked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kipper' is not the fish but one who kips.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormant spy is so called, and so is anyone slumbering, which is what a kipper does.

clue.text: Pen given the French name

parts.note: a pen for pigs is a sty
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A writing instrument is given its French title.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to name or title them, as in being styled a lord.

clue.text: When darkness falls, nocturnal insects go haywire — they all start together

indicators.note: the five words all begin at once, so their opening letters are taken in a row

explanation.surface: After sunset, moths and other creatures of the dark swarm wildly all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they' looks like a pronoun for the insects, but it is the fifth word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness after dusk are the time of day that the clue describes.

clue.text: "Hold the line"--that's a criminal offence

parts.note: to embrace someone is to hold them in your arms
RY is a crossword abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A telephone instruction to wait turns out to be illegal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold the line' reads as a phone request, but 'the' is just padding inside the quoted phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Embracery is the old crime of trying to bribe or sway a jury.

clue.text: Forward in fishing boat

definitions.meaning: in rugby, the player in the middle of the front row of the scrum, one of the forwards
a single-masted vessel used for fishing with hook and line, especially in Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone sits up at the bow of a trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugby player who hooks the ball in the scrum shares a name with an old Irish fishing vessel.

clue.text: Put back a pound in exes perhaps half a dozen times

indicators.note: in places the reversed word and the pound sign within the rearranged letters
perhaps hints that the four letters of exes may be arranged some other way
back says the word put is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Former partners keep putting money back into a deal six times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exes' suggests former partners, but here it is just four letters to rearrange; 'perhaps' is the anagram signal and 'back' the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixfold, or multiplied by six; six is half of twelve.

clue.text: Giant could give a gang a turn

indicators.note: could give says the following letters can be reworked to produce the answer

explanation.surface: A huge person might let a gang of children take turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantuan means enormous, from Rabelais's giant Gargantua.

clue.text: Greek character taking part in some games

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Greek athlete competes at the Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet is a character in that script.

clue.text: Amateur bitterly running for free

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are set in motion and end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A non-professional jogger complains bitterly about not being paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at liberty is to be unconfined, released from any restraint.

clue.text: Reverse boat's direction in stagnant pool

definitions.meaning: in rowing, to ... is to push the oars the other way to stop or go astern
a stretch of still water cut off from the current

explanation.surface: A rower turns around in still murky water.
explanation.definitionFit: Still water off the main stream is the noun sense; the rowing term is pushing the oars backward.

clue.text: Jaw from ox, yet unusual ox

parts.note: a yak is a Tibetan ox

indicators.note: unusual suggests the three letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: a second yak, the Tibetan ox

explanation.surface: A jawbone comes from an ox, and yet a strange ox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaw' is the verb to chatter, not the bone; 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To jaw is to talk at length, and incessant chatter is what the reduplicated phrase means.

clue.text: Illumination,/ almost plentiful, though pale round the edges

indicators.note: round the edges says one word wraps around another, its letters forming the border

parts.note: light colours are pale ones

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: ample means plentiful or more than enough

explanation.surface: A lamp gives off a lot of light, though it fades at the margins.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash after 'Illumination' is a mark on the scanned page, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Light given off by lamps, as in a street at night, is a form of illumination.

clue.text: Nancy gets as much money as possible from work

parts.words: gets as much money as possible from
parts.note: to milk a source is to extract all the money you can from it
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Nancy squeezes every penny she can out of her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a name, but it is a dated derogatory word for a weak, effeminate man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated insults for a timid, unmanly man.

clue.text: Keep tabs on an alien, using listening device

indicators.note: a listening device is an ear or a bug, so the word is taken as heard rather than as written

parts.note: a Czech, someone from the Czech Republic, is a foreigner or alien to a Briton

explanation.surface: Spies monitor a foreigner by planting a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alien' suggests space creatures, but it means a foreign national; the nationality chosen sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep tabs on someone is to monitor or inspect them.

clue.text: Blow up to set free

definitions.meaning: an archaic sense, to release from confinement

explanation.surface: An explosion releases someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something bigger is the usual sense; releasing a prisoner is an old legal one.

clue.text: A control used in the manufacture of dye

indicators.note: manufacture means making something new, so these letters are built into a different word

explanation.surface: A regulating device is part of the dye-making process.
explanation.definitionFit: A colorant is any substance that gives colour, such as a pigment or dye.

clue.text: Brisk, rising junior officer outlines how an' officer should be addressed

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the whole construction is read from bottom up
outlines means the officer's letters go around the form of address

parts.note: PC, police constable, is the lowest police rank

parts.words: how an' officer should be addressed
parts.note: an officer is addressed as sir

explanation.surface: A promoted constable briskly explains the right way to address a superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the whole assembled run, not just one piece. The apostrophe after 'an' is a mark on the scan.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisp means sharp and lively, as in a crisp manner.

clue.text: Crooked Ken said to make money

indicators.note: said signals that the words are taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: crooked is wry, and to ken is to know

explanation.surface: A dishonest man named Ken is reported to be making a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a name but is the Scottish verb to know.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old British slang for cash.

clue.text: Dim, foolish person left one inside

indicators.note: inside says the two short pieces go within the word for a fool

parts.note: a twit is a silly person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A stupid person kept one other indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' looks like it describes the foolish person, but it is the definition: half-lit, as at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit only faintly, as by twilight, so murky or shadowy.

clue.text: Part of speech, note, cut up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the trimmed word is read from bottom to top
cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson covers words, notes and being upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims BREVE to BREV and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An action word is one of the grammatical classes, the parts of speech.

clue.text: Found in its original place, about half of it, at the outside

indicators.note: about says the Latin phrase goes around the next piece

parts.note: in situ is the Latin phrase for in its original position

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is one letter, here its second
the outside of the word the is its first and last letters, attached at the end

explanation.surface: Something discovered where it lay, roughly half of it sticking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is the verb to establish, not a past tense. IN SITU goes round T (half of 'it'), then TE (the outside of 'the') is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute is to set up or establish, the same sense as founding a company.

clue.text: Stay covered in black stuff

definitions.meaning: smeared with tar, the black sticky substance used on roads

explanation.surface: Someone stays put while coated in something dark and sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Linger is the verb sense; the adjective means daubed with pitch, two unrelated words spelt alike.

clue.text: Copper in inferior canteen finally finds unsubstantial snack

indicators.note: in places the policeman inside the word for low quality

parts.note: poor means of low quality, inferior
PC, police constable, is a copper or policeman

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A policeman in a shabby works canteen ends up with a light snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests the metal Cu, but it is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffed maize kernels make a light, airy snack with little bulk.

clue.text: Frenzied — fool embraces 'is companion

indicators.note: embraces says the word for a fool holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: berk is British slang for an idiot
his companion would be hers; with the H dropped, as the apostrophe shows, it is 'ers

explanation.surface: An idiot wildly hugs his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe marks a dropped H, so 'his' is 'is and his companion, hers, becomes 'ers.
explanation.definitionFit: Going wild or out of control is a state of frenzy.
